title: Stop a rolling ball before it falls off the table, then put it in a cup
instruction: The ball is about to roll off the left edge of the table. Stop it before it falls, then put it in the blue cup.
context: Round things knocked over on a bench, cart or counter (a vial, fruit, a tool) roll toward the edge and break or hurt someone when they land; a robot working beside people must notice and stop them in time, then make them safe. Unlike tasks where the robot rolls a ball itself, here it can only react to a motion it didn't start.
setup: The two arm bases stand 61 cm apart on an oak table (1.10 x 1.30 m), whose left edge is 65 cm to the robot's left of the midpoint between the bases. A grey wooden ramp board (34 cm long, 10 cm wide) slopes down toward the left at 3 degrees, along a line 30 cm in front of the bases; its lower end meets the table (no step) 15 cm to the right of the midpoint, and its upper end is 1.8 cm above the table, 49 cm right of the midpoint. Two dark side rails (6 mm wide, 1.2 cm tall) run along its full length, 6.2 cm apart inside. An orange rubber ball (5 cm diameter, 60 g) rests on the ramp's centre line, its contact point 25 cm up the slope from the lower end, against a grey gate (6.2 x 1 x 5 cm plate across the chute, 2 mm above the ramp). A blue plastic cup (open square box, 10 x 10 cm outside, 8 x 8 cm inside, 1 cm floor, 4 cm tall walls) stands on the table, square to the table, its centre 17 cm in front of the bases and 22 cm left of the midpoint. Nothing else is on the table. At 1.0 s into the trial the gate lifts 6 cm straight up in 0.3 s and the ball rolls.
scoring: 1.0 if the ball ends in the cup: its centre inside the cup's walls, its underside within 1 cm of the cup floor, still for 1 s. Otherwise 0 if the ball fell off the table at any time (its centre 5 cm or more below the table top); else the best reached during the trial: 0.75 if its centre was at some point inside the cup's walls and below the rim; 0.5 if its underside was at some point 3 cm or more above the table top (picked up); 0.25 if it was at some point still (under 2 cm/s) for 0.5 s in a row, at least 2 cm from where it started (stopped); otherwise 0.
reset_notes: Lower the gate, put the ball back against it on the ramp's centre line, and lift the gate 1.0 s after the trial starts. Catch the ball under the left edge if it falls.
fidelity: The gate follows its path exactly (it can't be pushed). The ball is a rigid sphere with rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), no bounce and no rolling resistance, so it crosses the table at a near-constant 0.43 m/s and reaches the edge 3.0 s after the gate lifts (analytic); a real ball slows slightly and may bounce off the fingers. The ramp is a fixed tilted box meeting the table without a step. The roll timing is not measured directly in Isaac Sim, but the scripted demo, timed by it, stops the ball and scores 1.0 there.
